en: The Section on Detailed Exposition, Chapter Twelve: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Convergence of the Mode of Entry.
In this context, what is the convergence of the mode of entry?
It is the verse: “Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, the range of right intention.”
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, right intention is the range.
“Having right view as the foremost”: when right view is grasped, the five faculties are thereby grasped; this is the entry by way of the faculties. Those same faculties are true knowledge (*vijjā*);

with the arising of true knowledge, ignorance ceases; with the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease; with the cessation of volitional formations, consciousness ceases—and so on for everything. This is the entry by way of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*).
Those same five faculties are comprised within three aggregates:
the aggregate of virtue, the aggregate of concentration, and the aggregate of wisdom.
This is the entry by way of the aggregates.
Those same five faculties included within formations (*saṅkhāra*).

Those formations that are without taints (*anāsava*) and are not part of the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*), those formations are comprised within the element of mental phenomena (*dhammadhātu*); this is the entry by way of the elements.

That element of mental phenomena is included within the base of mental phenomena (*dhammāyatana*). That base which is without taints and is not part of the life-continuum; this is the entry by way of the bases.
The application of the method of entry through the modes of conveyance is concluded.
